notes.paraphrase: The intermediate annual obstacle system gives each of nine mewa a named mirror and category of purported misfortunes; White One is gods, Black Two demons, Blue Three attachment spirits, Green Four serpentine spirits, Yellow Five soil spirits, White Six king spirits, Red Seven haunting spirits, White Eight countryside deities, and Red Nine imprecatory goddesses.
notes.source_status: English translated/calculation summary; original Tibetan not collated

anchor.source: White Beryl chapter 24 ff.263b–273b; corresponding plates 9 and 18–19

notes.paraphrase: Besides the current-year mewa mirror's general reading, the text contrasts current and natal mewa, giving different purported ailments and ritual recommendations for color/element matches and mismatches.
notes.source_status: English translated/calculation summary; original Tibetan not collated

anchor.source: White Beryl chapter 24 ff.263b–273b; corresponding plates 9 and 18–19

notes.paraphrase: General numeric-square obstacles include a household-majority classification by numeric-square subsets, particularly White 1/6/8, Black 2/Blue 3, Green 4, Yellow 5, Red 7/9; group membership is necessary before its prediction.

known_limitations: Question-time input explicitly required for consultation-hour segment, cannot be inferred from birth time
Black Two with other mewa and repeated natal/current colors are symbolic claims only
Medical/disease/mortality statements are not scientifically validated clinical prognosis
Minor pebble statuses not independently reproduced using a complete traditional calendar engine
Different age-nine modes must be preserved as variants
